title: Common etale regular Hilbert coefficient datum
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $X,M$ schemes [def-pc-scheme], $p:M\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $i:X\to M$, $a\in X$, and $m,n,s,Q\in\mathbf N$, with ordered minimal vertices $\alpha_i\in\mathbf N^n$. A regular Hilbert coefficient datum consists of the following specified objects and properties (it does not assert that such objects exist). There is one affine etale neighbourhood $e:U\to M$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] and $a_U\in U$ above $i(a)$; an affine smooth closed $j:N\hookrightarrow U$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $b_0\in N$ mapping to $a_U$; etale regular coordinates $(w,z)$ on $U$ over $k$, with $w$ etale coordinates on $N$; and $n$ regular equations generating the ideal of $N$, with invertible transverse Jacobian everywhere on $N$. The coordinates respect $p$. Taylor maps to $\kappa(y)[[W,Z]]$ on $U$ and to $\kappa(b)[[W]]$ on $N$ [def-weil-residue-field] [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] are the homomorphisms whose residue map is evaluation, which send scalars to constants and coordinates to their value plus the corresponding formal variable. The straightened Taylor map sends $w$ to $w(b)+W$ and $z$ to $Z$ plus the Taylor series of $z|_N$, as in the implicit graph construction. The Taylor ideal is extension of the kernel of the restriction to $X\times_M U$. Choose regular functions $c_{i\gamma}$ on this same $N$ and series $f_{i,b}(W,Z)=\sum_\gamma T_b(c_{i\gamma})(W)Z^\gamma$ for all $b\in N$. At $b_0$, for the total-degree lexicographic order on exponents of $(W,Z)$ with the variables $W$ before $Z$, their first exponents are $(0,\alpha_i)$, in ascending total-degree lexicographic order. The $\alpha_i$ are pairwise incomparable for divisibility, and every transverse variable occurs in one of them; thus their orthants form a finite diagram with zero $W$ components. Put $d_i=|\alpha_i|$, and define $\Delta_i$ by assigning each exponent to its first vertex. Choose $i(j),\beta_j$ with $\alpha_{i(j)}=\beta_j+e_j$, in the first degree block containing $Z_j$. The point $b_0$ belongs to $S=\{b:\operatorname{ord}_b c_{i\gamma}\ge d_i-|\gamma|\text{ for }|\gamma|<d_i\}$. Here order of a regular function means that its germ lies in the indicated power of the local maximal ideal, so zero has infinite order. At every $b\in S$, writing $I_b$ for the straightened Taylor ideal, (1) $f_{i,b}\in I_b$ and $\operatorname{ord}f_{i,b}=d_i$; (2) for every degree-prefix bound $q$ and homogeneous degree $t$, every homogeneous polynomial has a unique sum of the initial forms of $f_{i,b}$ with $d_i\le q$, times homogeneous quotients of degree $t-d_i$ supported in $\Delta_i$, and a homogeneous remainder of degree $t$ outside the prefix diagram, with zero quotient when $t<d_i$; (3) every element of $I_b$ is $\sum_i q_i f_{i,b}$ with $\operatorname{supp}q_i\subset\Delta_i$; (4) for each degree block, put $Z^\ell$ equal to its prefix essential variables: $g_j=\partial_Z^{\beta_j} f_{i(j),b}$ belongs to $(Z^\ell)$ for $Z_j\in Z^\ell$, and the constant Jacobian determinant of these $g_j$ in those variables is a unit; (5) for each later $i$ and exponent $\delta$ in the prefix diagram restricted to $Z^\ell$, $|\delta|\le Q$, one has $\partial_{Z^\ell}^\delta f_{i,b}\in(Z^\ell)$. Formal derivatives are [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative]. Finally, at every $y\in U$ the function $q\mapsto\operatorname{length}(\kappa(y)[[W,Z]]/(I_y+(W,Z)^{q+1}))$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length] is pointwise at most its value at $a_U$. All relative variables are retained at nonclosed points, giving the extended Hilbert--Samuel convention. The empty vertex set and zero transverse variables are allowed.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), (7.1)--(7.2), Theorem 9.6 and Remark 9.9; ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13

reviewed_lean.note: H3 in new def RegularHilbertCoefficientDatum.first_minimal: Finsupp.DegLex (·<·)(·<·) on Fin m ⊕ Fin n uses Mathlib's Sum.instLTSum (LiftRel, W and Z incomparable), so Pi.Lex ignores the W part against the vertex (0,α) and forces W-monomial coefficients to vanish. The theorem is then false: for x²+y²+z²=0 in A³ at 0 (rank-3 tangent cone), every case n=0..3 gives a contradiction. Otherwise checked: item statement identical to live; stmt_deps only add the new def; hypotheses (CharZero, closed immersion, reduced, smooth, finite type) not stronger; canonical Taylor maps pinned by residue and coordinates (unique by formal étaleness); straightened map gives N={Z=0}; conditions (1)-(5), first-block pick, ∃diagram ∀Q≥max d_i−1 datum, pointwise extended Hilbert–Samuel bound; edge cases s=0, n=0, zero coefficients, t<d_i, nonclosed points; single universe u; H12 fields, docstrings and three search kinds OK; no sorry in defs.
